policy: Research bounty for a sponsor-selected public Arbitrum One receipt. Explain execution status, distinguish the transaction destination from its event emitter, and explain why a successful execution or observed log is not evidence of personal ownership or future reward entitlement. Ground specific facts in the normalized RPC receipt. Do not invent token symbols, decimals or function names. The researcher need not own the source wallet. One fixed award is allocated by first successful settlement.
reports: The selected Arbitrum receipt has status 1, meaning the execution succeeded rather than reverted. Its transaction destination is 0xaf88d065e77c8cc2239327c5edb3a432268e5831; the single log was emitted by that same address. The native transaction value is zero. Success describes this execution, not ownership by the researcher or a promise of future rewards. Raw event data alone does not establish a token symbol or decimals.

This receipt confirms successful execution and one event, whose emitting address matches the transaction destination 0xaf88d065e77c8cc2239327c5edb3a432268e5831. No native ETH value was attached. An observed event is a record of this transaction, not authorization for this reporter to claim assets. I do not infer current eligibility, token units or a named function merely from the log and input selector.
